clue.text: Animal taking a long time to become a bird

parts.note: an eon is an immensely long period

explanation.surface: A creature evolving over ages into something with wings.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests evolution; in fact the animal simply takes on a long period after it.
explanation.definitionFit: The pigeon is a common bird, the familiar city dove.

clue.text: Show forbearance

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a stage show, the Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera
second meaning: calm tolerance of delay or provocation

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as an instruction to be tolerant, but 'Show' is a noun naming a theatre piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Patience is a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta, and the word also means tolerant endurance.

clue.text: Avaricious king eagerly desiring to go out

parts.note: someone gasping to go out is eager to get away

explanation.surface: A greedy monarch keen to escape.
explanation.walkthrough: No word signals the insertion: the king just sits inside the desire.
explanation.definitionFit: Grasping means greedy for money or possessions, the same as avaricious.

clue.text: It's different to go up to the woman

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the word reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: taken as written, then read upwards

explanation.surface: Things change when you climb up to see a lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Other means distinct or not the same, a synonym for different.

clue.text: Girl Lawrence followed like a star

parts.note: T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia, known by his initials

explanation.surface: A young woman chasing after a celebrity named Lawrence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Followed' places Lawrence's initials after the girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Stellate is a formal adjective describing anything shaped or radiating like a star.

clue.text: Annexed unilaterally though prepared to talk privately

parts.note: to annex territory is to take it
unilateral action comes from one side alone

explanation.surface: A territory seized without agreement, yet the seizer is ready for quiet talks.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking someone on one side is drawing them aside for a private word.

clue.text: Yearn to be with a companion in Californian resort

explanation.surface: Wishing to holiday on the Californian coast with a partner.
explanation.walkthrough: CH is the British honour Companion of Honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Long Beach is a coastal city near Los Angeles, a seaside destination.

clue.text: Topless swimmer many see as nut

indicators.note: topless means the head is removed, so the first letter goes

explanation.surface: Seaside crowds staring at a topless bather and thinking them mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many' stands for a Roman numeral, here D for 500. 'Nut' looks like slang for a crazy person but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The almond is an edible nut, the seed of a tree related to the peach.

clue.text: Emit smell though formerly sound

parts.note: sound in the sense of healthy

explanation.surface: Giving off an odour despite once being in good health.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhale is to breathe out or give off vapour or scent.

clue.text: Create a character partly to impart information to people

indicators.note: only part of the run of words is used, so the answer sits inside them

parts.note: found across the end of the first word, the article and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A novelist inventing a character in order to put a message across to readers.
explanation.definitionFit: To instruct is to pass on knowledge to others, which is what teaching does.

clue.text: Allen taking final curtain at speed — elusive creature!

indicators.note: the comedian's name takes in a letter, holding it within itself
final asks for only the closing letter of the word that follows

parts.note: speed is measured in miles per hour

explanation.surface: Woody Allen bringing the curtain down in a hurry, then a startled exclamation about a shy animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter goes inside the comedian's first name, before its last letter, and the speed unit follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A wood nymph is a dryad, a forest spirit of myth glimpsed but never caught.

clue.text: Attended sporting occasion and was ruined

definitions.meaning: first meaning: went to greyhound racing
second meaning: the idiom for decline into ruin

explanation.surface: A punter who spent a day at the races and lost everything.
explanation.walkthrough: Greyhound racing is called 'the dogs' in Britain and Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for falling into ruin also literally describes going to a greyhound meeting.

clue.text: Note spare construction of auxiliary language

indicators.note: a construction is something built up from parts, so these letters are assembled anew

parts.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: An instruction to make a backup note while building an international language.
explanation.definitionFit: Esperanto was invented as an international second language, the best-known constructed auxiliary tongue.

clue.text: Commonplace to put prohibition on a learner

parts.note: L for learner, as on a British L-plate for learner drivers

explanation.surface: It is routine to forbid a learner driver from doing something.
explanation.definitionFit: Banal and commonplace are synonyms for something trite and unoriginal.

clue.text: For Capone to attend assembly is customary

explanation.surface: It is the usual thing for a gangster to turn up at a gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: Al attends the assembly by standing next to it, at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Conventional means following usual practice, exactly what customary describes.

clue.text: Leader turning out liar at no time

indicators.note: turning out suggests something being turned over and reworked, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: tide is an old word for time or season, as in Christmastide

explanation.surface: A head of state who never once proves to be a liar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At no time' looks like one phrase meaning never; it splits into a link word, O and TIDE. Read backwards the string is nearly the answer, but the A and I of liar must swap, so it is a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: In British newspapers the leader, or leading article, is the editorial voicing the paper's own opinion.

clue.text: Thieves commonly said to take ladies' underwear

indicators.note: said means we go by how the word is pronounced

parts.note: nicker is colloquial British for a thief, from nick, to steal

explanation.surface: Common thieves are reported to steal women's lingerie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commonly' marks slang: to nick is British for to steal.
explanation.definitionFit: Knickers are women's underpants in British usage.

clue.text: Southern priests sticking to lasts

indicators.note: a loose signal: the letters of these words stick together and then are rearranged

explanation.surface: Clergy in the south clinging to the shoemaker's lasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sticking' is an unusual signal to rearrange; the letters of S plus priests rebuild the answer exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: To persist is to continue or endure, which is the verb sense of lasts.

clue.text: More or less the same as small coins

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a few low-value coins in the pocket

explanation.surface: Saying something is about equal in value to a handful of loose coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' means both alteration and coins; 'little' qualifies each sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation with little alteration is roughly unaltered, and a few low-value coins are a small amount of loose money.

clue.text: Achieves success with musical compositions

definitions.meaning: first meaning: wins, hits the target

explanation.surface: A composer finding fame through their works.
explanation.definitionFit: To score is to succeed, and scores are the written music of compositions.

clue.text: Proceed to call in on non-native speaker in Mexico

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

explanation.surface: Visiting a foreigner in Mexico after phoning ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Gringo is the Latin American term for a foreigner, especially an English-speaking one.

clue.text: Goods carried in first colonial vessel

indicators.note: first asks for just the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: the Argo, the ship of Jason and the Argonauts

explanation.surface: Merchandise brought over in the earliest ship of a colony.
explanation.definitionFit: Cargo is the freight or goods carried by a ship or aircraft.

clue.text: See scene-playing out of show

indicators.note: playing out suggests a performance unfolding freely, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: vide is Latin for see, used in references

explanation.surface: Watching a scene being acted out in a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' becomes Latin VIDE, as in a footnote's 'vide p. 12', before joining the letters of scene.
explanation.definitionFit: To evidence something is to demonstrate or display it, so evidences works as the verb shows.

clue.text: Praise letter many rejected

parts.note: the spelt-out name of a letter of the alphabet

indicators.note: rejected suggests being sent back, so the word is read the other way

explanation.surface: A letter of praise that most people turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise enthusiastically, so the two are synonymous verbs.

clue.text: Scold one European for being wild wreckless person

parts.note: to rant is to rail at someone

explanation.surface: Telling off a foreigner for behaving recklessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wreckless' plays on reckless: a rantipole is a wild, unruly person.
explanation.definitionFit: Rantipole is an old word for a wild, rakish, ill-behaved person, a tearaway.

clue.text: Rows leading to weeping aloud

indicators.note: aloud means we hear the word spoken rather than see it spelt

parts.note: weeping produces drops from the eyes

explanation.surface: Quarrels that end with someone crying out loud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rows' looks like arguments, but it is the definition in the sense of lines of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiers are rows set one above another, as in a theatre or stadium.

clue.text: Untainted place on the French ship

explanation.surface: A clean berth aboard a French vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spotless is unblemished and pure, free of any stain or taint.

clue.text: Embraces soft form outside

indicators.note: outside means one word sits around the other, wrapping it

parts.note: a school form is a class
p for piano, soft in music

explanation.surface: Hugs from a gentle shape held all around.
explanation.definitionFit: To clasp someone is to hold them tightly, an embrace.
